attentionDate.def: When someone should look at this again, whatever else happens before then.
attentionDate.label: Attention date
attentionDate.not: a deadline or a reminder to do the work itself.
capacityAdjustment.def: A change to this quarter only, with the reason recorded beside it.
capacityAdjustment.eg: Minus ten units for a vacancy, or plus five for a returning secondee.
capacityAdjustment.label: Adjustment
capacityAdjustment.not: a permanent change to the team’s size.
capacityBaseline.def: What this team can normally deliver in a quarter, before anything is set aside.
capacityBaseline.label: Baseline capacity
carryOver.def: Capacity that arrived from an earlier quarter because the work did not finish.
carryOver.eg: Ten units carried from Q2 are consuming Q3, not being planned into it.
carryOver.label: Carried over
carryOver.not: new demand. It was already committed; it simply moved.
class.def: Why this work exists: mandatory, strategic, operational, or discretionary.
class.eg: A regulatory deadline is Mandatory whatever anyone thinks of it.
class.label: Class
class.not: a priority ranking. Two mandatory items can still have different importance.
deliverable.def: What is left for committed work once reserves are taken off.
deliverable.label: Deliverable capacity
dependencyStatus.def: Whether the dependency is open, at risk, or resolved.
dependencyStatus.label: Dependency status
dependencyStatus.not: a measure of how hard it will be to resolve.
dependencyType.def: What this work needs from something else: capacity, a delivery, a decision, or an approval.
dependencyType.label: Dependency type
dependencyType.not: a statement of blame or of ordering on a plan.
externalLink.def: A typed pointer to the record that lives elsewhere — a ticket, a document, a dashboard.
externalLink.eg: Links must be https, and open in your browser rather than inside Flowmap.
externalLink.label: Link
externalLink.not: a copy of that record. Flowmap stores the address, never the contents.
importance.def: How much it matters relative to everything else in the portfolio.
importance.label: Importance
importance.not: urgency. Something can matter greatly and not be needed for a year.
isHard.def: A dependency that stops the work outright if it is not met.
isHard.label: Hard dependency
isHard.not: a dependency that is merely inconvenient. Blocked-by and approvals are hard by default.
latestSafeStart.def: The last date this can begin and still land on its target.
latestSafeStart.eg: Past this date the target is at risk whether or not anything has gone wrong.
latestSafeStart.label: Latest safe start
latestSafeStart.not: when it is scheduled to start.
lifecycle.def: Where this work has got to: an idea, committed, in delivery, done, on hold, or dropped.
lifecycle.eg: Committed means capacity has been set aside, not that anyone has started.
lifecycle.label: Lifecycle
lifecycle.not: a progress percentage, or a measure of how well it is going.
managementNote.def: Context for whoever picks this up next, capped at two thousand characters.
managementNote.label: Management note
managementNote.not: a place for credentials, customer data, incident detail, or anything you would not put in an export.
milestone.def: A checkable point inside this work, capped at six so the list stays a summary.
milestone.label: Milestone
milestone.not: a task list or a project plan.
name.def: What this piece of work is called, in the words the organisation already uses for it.
name.label: Name
neededBy.def: When this dependency has to be resolved for the work to stay on target.
neededBy.label: Needed by
nextAction.def: The single next thing that has to happen, and who has to do it.
nextAction.label: Next action
nextAction.not: a plan. One step, named, with an owner.
outcome.def: What will be true once this is done, stated so someone outside the team could check it.
outcome.eg: “Merchants can request payment in-app”, not “build the request-to-pay service”.
outcome.label: Outcome
outcome.not: a list of deliverables or a description of the work.
overflow.def: How much more is committed than the deliverable capacity can hold.
overflow.label: Over capacity
overflow.not: a failure state. It is a fact to decide about, and it never blocks a change.
owner.def: The person or team accountable for this work reaching its outcome.
owner.label: Owner
owner.not: whoever happens to be doing it this week.
primaryTeam.def: The team that carries the main weight of this work, and where its primary footprint sits.
primaryTeam.eg: A payments change led by Payments with a slice of Security time.
primaryTeam.label: Primary team
primaryTeam.not: the only team involved. Work can occupy several teams at once.
productImpact.def: How much this work changes a given product or service: primary, major, minor, or a dependency.
productImpact.eg: Exactly one product may be Primary — the one this work is mostly about.
productImpact.label: Product impact
productImpact.not: a measure of effort. A minor change to a fragile product can still be hard.
reserves.def: Capacity held back before any work is placed: support, refinement, holidays, or holds.
reserves.label: Reserves
reserves.not: contingency for overruns. It is capacity already spoken for.
scopeConfidence.def: How sure the team is that what is being asked for will not grow.
scopeConfidence.label: Scope confidence
scopeConfidence.not: a measure of how well the requirements are written.
sizeConfidence.def: How sure the team is that the units are about right.
sizeConfidence.label: Size confidence
sizeConfidence.not: how likely the work is to succeed.
targetDate.def: A specific date, when there is one. Setting it derives the target quarter.
targetDate.label: Target date
targetDate.not: a promise unless the class says so — a mandatory item needs one to pass the gate.
targetQuarter.def: The quarter this work is aimed at finishing in.
targetQuarter.eg: Work can occupy two quarters of capacity and still target the second.
targetQuarter.label: Target quarter
targetQuarter.not: a commitment to a date, and not the same as where its capacity sits.
themes.def: Cross-cutting labels used to see the portfolio a different way.
themes.label: Themes
themes.not: a hierarchy or a programme structure. Work can carry several.
timingConfidence.def: How sure the team is that the target quarter will hold.
timingConfidence.label: Timing confidence
units.def: Approximate share of one team’s quarter this work occupies.
units.eg: Twenty units of a hundred is about a fifth of that team’s quarter.
units.label: Units
units.not: a story-point or person-day estimate, and not a measure of effort spent.
utilisation.def: Committed load as a share of deliverable capacity.
utilisation.eg: Over a hundred per cent is allowed and drawn — it means more is committed than fits.
utilisation.label: Utilisation
utilisation.not: a productivity measure, and not a target to maximise.
valueDrivers.def: The reasons this work is worth doing, drawn from the workspace’s agreed list.
valueDrivers.label: Value drivers
valueDrivers.not: a business case or a benefits calculation.
timingConfidence.not: a probability, and not a commitment to the date.
refinementLink.label: Ideas supported
refinementLink.def: Ideas this refinement reserve is shaping this quarter.
refinementLink.not: an allocation. The link carries no units and creates no placement.
refinementLink.eg: Refinement 5 units, supporting 3 Ideas — the 5 units pay for the shaping, not for any one Idea.
split.label: Split across quarters
split.def: Divides this placement, keeping the total the same.
split.not: a way to change how big the work is. Resize does that.
split.eg: 20 units in Q3 becomes 12 in Q3 and 8 in Q4.
rowOrder.label: Row order
rowOrder.def: The order teams appear down the map, set by a Planner.
rowOrder.not: a ranking, a priority, or anything the map changes on its own.
